title: The bread of life part 2
scripture_text: ‘’When they found him on the other side of the lake, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you get here?” Jesus answered, “Very truly I tell you, you are looking for me, not because you saw the signs I performed but because you ate the loaves and had your fill. Do not work for food that spoils, but for food that endures to eternal life. which the Son of Man will give you. For on him God the Father has placed his seal of approval.” Then they asked him, “What must we do to do the works God requires?”
devotional:
Jesus answered, “The work of God is this: to believe in the one he has sent. So they asked him, “What sign then will you give that we may see it and believe you?’ What will you do? Our ancestors ate the manna in the wilderness; as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from he haven to eat.’ Jesus said to them, “Very truly I tell you, it is not Moses who has given you the bread from heaven, but it is my Father who gives you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is the bread that comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” “Sir,” they said, “always give us this bread.” Then Jesus declared, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believe in me will never be thirsty. But as I told you, you have seen me and still you do not believe. All those the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never drive away. For I have come down from heaven not to do my will but to do the will of him who sent me. And this is the will of him who sent me, that I shall lose none of all those he has given me, but raise them up at the last day. For my Father’s will is that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in him shall have eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day.” John 6 v 25-40

‘’Jesus said to them, “Very truly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day. For my flesh is real food and my blood is real drink. Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in them. Just as the living Father sent me and I live because of the Father, so the one who feeds on me will live because of me. This is the bread that came down from heaven. Your ancestors ate manna and died, but whoever feeds on this bread will live forever.” He said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum. it, many of his disciples said, “This is a hard teaching. Who can accept it?”

Aware that his disciples were grumbling about this, Jesus said to them, “Does this offend you? Then what if you see the Son of Man ascend to where he was before! The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing. The words I have spoken to you—they are full of the Spirit and life. Yet there are some of you who do not believe.” For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray him. He went on to say, “This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless the Father has enabled them.” From this time many of his disciples turned back and no longer followed him.’’ John 6 v 53-66

Jesus exposes their motives

‘When they found him on the other side of the lake, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you get here?” Jesus answered, “Very truly I tell you, you are looking for me, not because you saw the signs I performed but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.’

The question the people asked Jesus “Rabbi, when did you get here?” may appear innocent enough, but we must read it in the context of what happened the previous day when they wanted to take Jesus by force and make him King. Jesus refused to be controlled or manipulated by them.

Jesus does not answer their question. He says something very strong and very confrontational, ‘Very truly I tell you.’ The words ‘very truly,’ or truly, truly, in the older versions, are used 25 times in John and was used when Jesus was going to say something very important. And then he says, ‘you are looking for me, not because you saw the signs I performed but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.’

The Message reads “You’ve come looking for me not because you saw God in my actions but because I fed you, filled your stomachs—and for free.”

These people were following Jesus with wrong selfish motives, and Jesus was not going to allow it. They wanted to be with Jesus because of what he could do for them, not because they wanted to know and love him. It is like getting married to someone not because you love them, but because they can do something for you. In the light of this passage, we need to conclude that Jesus is interested in our motive for following him.

Why do you want to follow Jesus?

Why do you want to live for God?

Some may think that if you are doing the right thing, and following Jesus then surely motive is not important.

Look at these words by A W Tozer: -

‘‘The test by which all conduct must finally be judged is motive. As water cannot rise higher than its source, so the moral quality in an act can never be higher than the motive that inspires it. For this reason, no act that arises from an evil motive can be good, even though some good may appear to come out of it. Every deed done out of anger or spite, for instance, will be found at last to have been done for the enemy and against the Kingdom of God. Unfortunately, the nature of religious activity is such that much of it can be carried on for reasons that are not good, such as anger, jealousy, ambition, vanity and avarice. All such activity is essentially evil and will be counted as such at the judgment.’’ tps://acts2024ministries.wordpress.com/tag/tozer

Motives are important because they are all about our hearts, and following Jesus is all about the heart. Many people give up their Christian faith because their motivation has been about using Jesus not knowing and loving Him. When their expectations are not met, they get frustrated and angry and they walk away.

Jesus redirects their focus.

“Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that lasts for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you, because God the Father has set his seal on him.”

In some ways these words redefine our humanity and go against our cultural and social norms. We live in a world where we are taught that our significance, identity and security are all tied up in our work. Work is a good thing and a gift from God, but the focus of our lives must be primarily on our spiritual lives.

Do you remember when Jesus was hungry in the wilderness, Satan tempted him to turn stones into bread. Basically, he was saying ‘Jesus use your power to meet your own needs, it is not God’s will for you to be hungry.’ Jesus’ reply was amazing. He quoted Deuteronomy 8;3 ’Man does not live on bread alone, but on every word, that comes from the mouth of God.’

This is what Jesus is saying to these people. ‘you need more than bread, you need more than having your material needs met, you need to grasp the fact that your humanity is created for intimacy with God and that is what you should be labouring at.

Our jobs have a measure of importance and we should do our best in our work to bring glory to God, however, if we take them too seriously, and they become essential for our identity and significance, then we will not have the heart or energy to labour for the bread that does not spoil.

Remember Jesus is speaking to people who had very little, they were poor people, yet their poverty did not excuse them from having a materialistic attitude.

This principle needs to govern our lives. The quality of the lives we live is not dependent upon the possessions we possess, or the things we achieve, but upon us allowing the word of God to nourish and transform us.
prayer: Father please expose in me any wrong motive for following you.
